title: Slipstream Neon

selected_categories.reasoning: The play space is clearly divided into three readable lanes, and success depends on shifting into safe lanes as enemy traffic spawns and descends.
The run has no finish line, score rises continuously with survival time/distance, and the session ends only when the player collides with an obstacle.
The mechanical structure is runner-like, and the presentation strongly emphasizes neon sci-fi colors, glowing lanes, and a cyberpunk night atmosphere.
The visuals and player fantasy resemble traffic racing or futuristic road racing, but there are no opponents to overtake by placement, no laps, and no finish state.
The game becomes about enduring higher speed and tighter reaction windows, though it lacks the usual level-completion or route-optimization structure associated with speedrunning.

uncertainty_notes: The game visually suggests a car or interceptor racer, but its actual rules are closer to obstacle-dodging survival than traditional racing.
The player can move continuously across the road rather than snapping strictly by lane, so 'Lane runner game' is the best abstract fit rather than a perfect literal label.
No shooting, combat, collection, or upgrade systems are present, reducing fit with broader action or progression-heavy categories.
